name: BEBC / WA66 beam-dump run
full_name: Big European Bubble Chamber — WA66 beam-dump search
summary: BEBC / WA66 beam-dump run operated in CERN's historical West Area at BEBC. BEBC is the host detector and WA66 the specific beam program; they are grouped to avoid double counting.
detection_principle: New particles from a high-energy proton dump can cause forward-electron scattering in a downstream bubble chamber; the old event sample is reanalyzed in modern dark-sector models.

status.label: 1982 WA66 beam-dump sample, reinterpreted in 2020
status.evidence: Status follows the listed sources and the eras of their data/proposals; the access date is not confirmation of new operation.

collaboration.name: BEBC / WA66 beam-dump run Collaboration / project team

key_parameters.name: Type of dark-sector analysis
key_parameters.value: Theoretical reinterpretation of historical WA66 electron-scattering data, rather than a new run

results.summary: Limits were obtained for millicharged and electromagnetic-dipole light dark matter, extending to GeV scales in some regions.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered. This record includes reinterpretations of historical data in new models. A reinterpretation paper's publication year is not the apparatus operating year, and the original experiment may primarily have targeted neutrinos, axions or other light particles.
